steps.what: Evaluate students' work against economics reasoning and the assignment rubric
Write feedback explaining strengths, errors and suggested improvements

loop.purpose: Draft feedback from the instructor's own assessment
loop.input: Assessment notes and relevant student passages
loop.check: Verify that feedback accurately describes the student's reasoning and the instructor's intended advice
loop.stop: One draft and correction; unclear or unsupported comments are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining reasoning errors requires contextual language beyond standard comments

steps.what: Decide the grade and finalize feedback for the assessed work

tasks.design: Use the {LMS} feedback function to draft prose from the teacher's assessment notes. Keep reading, economic reasoning assessment and every grade decision with the teacher; official record transfer is a separate task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing individualized feedback repeated reasoning already captured in assessment notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Instructor-note-based feedback drafting can propose text for checking.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible comment may miss the student's argument or imply the wrong severity.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher distinguishes a defensible alternative argument from a conceptual error.
tasks.altitude: Limited feedback-writing time returns to examining student reasoning.

reach.task: Prepare evidence-based feedback under an examiner's direction

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes; it does not establish autonomous grades or a local time saving.
Model knowledge: the conservative feedback-writing estimate is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers non-exam assignments, academic evaluation and final feedback; official record transfer and examination marking are separately owned.

The teacher produces s1 notes with assignment version, rubric criterion, quoted passage, reasoning issue and intended feedback. Capture and reading remain fully counted; missing passages or uncertain assessment require manual feedback rather than generated grades.
Test native feedback comments and templates before adding a model; do not automate grade decisions.
Four incremental focal hours cover feedback instruction checks and sample audits.
unknowns: Existing feedback tools and institutional policy
research_questions: Does checked feedback drafting reduce total marking time without changing academic judgement?

incremental.description: Maintain instructions and audit feedback samples

approvals.approved_version: Exact student submission, rubric version, grade and feedback text; changes void approval

tasks.short: Revise economics curricula and teaching methods

steps.what: Evaluate curricula, learning outcomes and evidence about the effectiveness of instruction
Draft revised course content, materials and proposed methods of instruction

loop.purpose: Draft revised teaching material within explicit outcomes and source constraints
loop.input: Revision brief and verified source passages
loop.output: Course revision draft with an outcome map
loop.check: Solve example problems and verify economic claims, prerequisites and outcome alignment
loop.stop: One draft and correction; unresolved content returns to teacher authorship
loop.why_not_simpler: Reworking explanations and activities requires contextual writing; templates only structure the document

steps.what: Choose revisions and finalize the course design for programme review

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates and a bounded drafting loop to propose revised course material from teacher-defined outcomes. The teacher validates examples, chooses instructional changes and submits the proposal through the existing programme process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Revision required repeated rewriting after substantive course decisions were formed.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can propose alternative explanations and exercises.
tasks.still_hard: Curriculum coherence, difficulty and instructional effectiveness require educational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher understands misconceptions and prerequisites that shape student learning.
tasks.altitude: Limited rewriting time returns to checking sequence and conceptual depth.

reach.task: Map course activities to programme outcomes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded drafting of economics course material is plausible; no local curriculum-development saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary ends at the teacher's course proposal; committee approval, teaching delivery and subsequent evaluation are separately owned.

The teacher produces s1 outcomes, prerequisites, constraints, revision rationale, selected evidence and source versions. Capture and evaluation remain counted; gaps and unresolved examples return to manual development rather than assumed alignment flags.
Use existing document templates and reusable teaching material before custom drafting.
Four incremental focal hours cover source and instruction maintenance.
unknowns: Current revision frequency and reusable material
research_questions: Does checked drafting preserve correct examples and outcome coverage while reducing rewriting?

already_counted.description: Check drafted content and solve examples

incremental.description: Maintain source set and drafting instructions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R91.25 gives8.75 gross minus4 upkeep =4.75 net. Major curriculum redesign or examples needing rework support only0-2% conservative saving.

tasks.short: Compile, administer and grade economics examinations

steps.what: Compile examinations, verify scoring rules and administer the assessment
Score closed examination questions against the verified answer key
Grade open answers, investigate scoring exceptions and decide final examination results

tasks.design: Configure closed-question marking in {LMS} using teacher-verified scoring rules. Keep examination design, administration, open-answer judgement and final decisions fully counted; official grade transfer follows as a separate task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some closed answers still required repeated manual key comparisons.
tasks.enabler_now: Native assessment functions can apply explicit scoring keys deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Economic arguments, ambiguous questions and disputed scoring require examiner judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognizes a valid argument that does not match a model answer.
tasks.altitude: Routine key comparison may shrink while attention stays on ambiguous answers and test validity.

evidence.claim: Ans supports automatic closed-question marking; this does not establish autonomous evaluation of open economics answers.
Model knowledge: savings depend on closed-question scoring still being manual.

assumptions: Boundary is examinations only, excluding non-exam assignments and official record transfer. The scenario is a teacher who performs the marking, so no assistant labour is silently removed.

In counted s1 the teacher verifies item identifiers, allowed responses, points, scoring-key version and roster mapping. Students produce responses during the administered exam; the teacher checks the submission manifest after collection. Missing identities, unsupported response formats or disputed keys go to manual marking.
Test native assessment configuration first; existing automatic marking earns no new labour credit.
Eight incremental focal hours cover key testing and scoring audits.
unknowns: Closed-question share and current automatic marking
research_questions: Can configured scoring reproduce examiner-checked scores while isolating missing or ambiguous responses?

already_counted.description: Examination preparation, scoring-key capture and administration
Open grading, exceptions and final decisions

incremental.description: Test scoring keys and audit results

approvals.approved_version: Exact submissions, scoring-key version, exception corrections and final examination decisions; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R80 gives20 gross minus8 upkeep =12 net. Essay-heavy exams or already automatic closed marking support only0-3% conservative saving.

tasks.short: Maintain attendance and official student records

steps.what: Capture attendance and reconcile required records with examiner-approved grade decisions
Copy attendance, grades and required fields into the official record draft
Resolve transfer exceptions and finalize the required student records

tasks.design: Configure a checked batch transfer from {LMS} to the {OTHER} student information system. The teacher retains attendance capture, identity reconciliation, exception handling and final record confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Grades and attendance were copied into a second official record system.
tasks.enabler_now: Native imports or supported connectors can reuse checked records without retyping them.
tasks.still_hard: Identity mismatches, corrected decisions and conflicting record versions require human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognizes when a technically valid transfer represents the wrong student or decision.
tasks.altitude: Some duplicate entry time returns to resolving genuine record discrepancies.

evidence.claim: The digest describes Radboud's requirement to publish Brightspace grades in OSIRIS as well; it establishes a dual-record context, not automatic local savings.
Model knowledge: configured record transfer can remove remaining duplicate entry after explicit capture and mapping.

assumptions: Boundary is record maintenance after academic grade decisions; the grading tasks own assessment time and no grading saving is counted again.

The teacher produces checked s1 fields: student identifier, course, assessment or session identifier, attendance status and date, approved grade, decision version and correction reference. Attendance capture and mapping verification remain counted. The examiner produces grades before this transfer begins; missing decisions or unmatched identities return to manual reconciliation.
The {OTHER} category is a student information system. Test native imports and connectors first; existing sync runtime earns no new saving.
Seven incremental focal hours cover mapping reviews and correction audits; four other-role hours cover connector and access upkeep.
unknowns: Actual duplicate entry and supported interfaces
Official record authority and correction rules
research_questions: Does a checked transfer preserve identity and decision version while reducing total record entry?

approvals.approved_version: Exact student identifiers, sessions, assessments, attendance statuses, grades and decision versions in the final batch; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R60 gives40 gross minus7 focal upkeep =33 net. Existing integration or frequent corrections support only0-8% conservative saving; capture and grade decisions remain fully counted.
